name: forge_mod
description: A small fictional NeoForge 1.21.1 mod (examples/forge_mod), shaped differently from glow_mod: Java and Kotlin code (DeferredRegister registries, a forge block with a ticking block entity, a menu and its Kotlin screen, a custom emberforge:forging recipe type and serializer, a client-to-server payload, a ModConfigSpec common config, @SubscribeEvent handlers, Kotlin commands), a data pack (forging/smelting/crafting recipes, item/block/biome tags, loot tables, a configured + placed ore feature, a NeoForge biome modifier, an advancement, two functions), assets (blockstates, block/item models, en_us / tr_tr translations), a documented default config/emberforge-common.toml and JUnit tests; no reference tree. 14 questions, 7 Turkish and 7 English: callers x3, cross_layer x4, config x2, resources x2, flow, behaviour, where.
verified_by: Gold facts were written by reading every file of examples/forge_mod line by line; every source.at line was re-read by hand after the example was finished, and each fact's source.at/source.contains pair is re-checked against the benchmark copy before any approach is scored (metrics.validate_gold).

provenance.questions_written_by: an agent asked by the Verinoda maintainer to write examples/forge_mod and this set in one session; it never ran Verinoda on the example and saw no Verinoda output for it or for these questions
provenance.gold_written_by: same agent, by reading every file of examples/forge_mod; checked with metrics.validate_gold only
provenance.example_written_by: same agent, same session, before the questions; written fresh after examples/glow_mod had been used for tuning, with a different loader (NeoForge), language mix (Java + Kotlin) and data shape (worldgen, biome modifier, custom recipe type)
provenance.caveat: held out for Verinoda's retrieval on these questions (no Verinoda run and no Verinoda output while writing the example or the set), but not independent of the design: the Minecraft support (resource ids, data-pack linking, Java calls, Turkish questions) was developed against other mods by the same project (a private mod and examples/glow_mod), and the author knew which kinds of features Verinoda supports when choosing what the example and the questions exercise

facts.fact: EmberNetwork.handleStoke, the server handler of StokeForgePayload, calls forge.stoke(player) once the player has that forge's menu open and is within 8 blocks (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/network/EmberNetwork.java:39)
EmberForgeBlock.useItemOn calls forge.stoke(player) when the block is right-clicked with a Forge Hammer, then damages the hammer (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlock.java:83)

negatives.statement: the client screen calls stoke itself (EmberForgeScreen.requestStoke only sends StokeForgePayload)

facts.fact: EmberForgeBlockEntity.serverTick adds a burnt fuel item's heat: HeatMath.addHeat(forge.heat, fuelHeat) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:82)
serverTick adds 2 heat every 40 game ticks while the block below is in #emberforge:forge_heat_sources (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:86-87)
EmberForgeBlockEntity.stoke adds stoke_heat: HeatMath.addHeat(heat, EmberConfig.STOKE_HEAT.get()) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:141)
inside the Kotlin object, the two-argument addHeat calls the three-argument overload with max_heat (src/main/kotlin/net/ashvale/emberforge/heat/HeatMath.kt:22)
the JUnit test HeatMathTest.heatStaysBetweenZeroAndTheMaximum calls the three-argument addHeat (src/test/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/HeatMathTest.java:21-25)

negatives.statement: EmberNetwork.handleStoke calls HeatMath.addHeat directly (it calls forge.stoke)
EmberForgeBlock.useItemOn calls HeatMath.addHeat directly (it calls forge.stoke)

questions.question: emberforge:forging tarif tipi kodda nerede tanımlanıyor ve bu tarifleri hangi kod okuyup kullanıyor?
questions.question_en: Where is the emberforge:forging recipe type defined in code, and which code reads and uses those recipes?

facts.fact: ModRecipes registers the recipe type "forging" in the emberforge RECIPE_TYPES register (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/registry/ModRecipes.java:18-19)
ModRecipes registers ForgingRecipe.Serializer as the "forging" recipe serializer (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/registry/ModRecipes.java:20-21)
ForgingRecipe.Serializer's CODEC reads the JSON fields ingredient, result, forge_time (default 200) and min_heat (default 0) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/recipe/ForgingRecipe.java:63-68)

EmberForgeBlockEntity.serverTick looks the input up with getRecipeFor(ModRecipes.FORGING_TYPE.get(), new SingleRecipeInput(input), level) and forges with the match (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:91-101)

data recipe cinder_ingots_from_forging.json is of this type: #emberforge:cinder_ores -> 2 emberforge:cinder_ingot, forge_time 160, min_heat 40 (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/recipe/cinder_ingots_from_forging.json:1-12)
data recipe forge_hammer.json is of this type: emberforge:cinder_ingot -> emberforge:forge_hammer, forge_time 400, min_heat 120 (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/recipe/forge_hammer.json:1-12)

negatives.statement: cinder_ingot_from_smelting.json is a forging recipe (it is minecraft:smelting)

questions.question: Where is the #emberforge:forge_fuels tag defined, what does it contain, and which code checks it?

facts.fact: the item tag file src/main/resources/data/emberforge/tags/item/forge_fuels.json lists minecraft:coal, minecraft:charcoal and minecraft:blaze_rod (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/tags/item/forge_fuels.json:3-7)

the Java TagKey is ModTags.FORGE_FUELS = itemTag("forge_fuels"), built with ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(EmberForge.MOD_ID, name) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/registry/ModTags.java:12, 16-18)
Kotlin HeatMath.heatForFuel returns 0 unless the stack is in ModTags.FORGE_FUELS, otherwise heat_per_fuel (double for a blaze rod) (src/main/kotlin/net/ashvale/emberforge/heat/HeatMath.kt:15-19)
EmberForgeMenu's fuel slot only accepts stacks in ModTags.FORGE_FUELS (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/menu/EmberForgeMenu.java:43-48)
through HeatMath.heatForFuel, EmberForgeBlockEntity.serverTick burns the fuel slot only when the item is in the tag (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:78-84)

negatives.statement: a forging recipe uses #emberforge:forge_fuels as its ingredient
EmberForgeBlockEntity.serverTick tests the tag itself (it asks HeatMath.heatForFuel)

questions.question: Cüruf cevheri dünyada hangi biyomlarda ve nasıl oluşuyor?
questions.question_en: In which biomes, and how, is cinder ore generated in the world?

facts.fact: the NeoForge biome modifier neoforge/biome_modifier/add_cinder_ore.json (neoforge:add_features) adds the placed feature emberforge:ore_cinder to the biomes in #emberforge:has_cinder_ore at step underground_ores (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/neoforge/biome_modifier/add_cinder_ore.json:2-5)

the biome tag has_cinder_ore lists #minecraft:is_badlands, minecraft:stony_peaks and minecraft:windswept_gravelly_hills (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/tags/worldgen/biome/has_cinder_ore.json:3-7)

the placed feature emberforge:ore_cinder tries 6 times per chunk (count 6, in_square), at heights 0 to 64 (trapezoid), filtered by biome (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/worldgen/placed_feature/ore_cinder.json:2-26)

it places the configured feature emberforge:ore_cinder: a minecraft:ore vein of size 7 of emberforge:cinder_ore replacing #minecraft:stone_ore_replaceables, 25% discarded on air exposure (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/worldgen/configured_feature/ore_cinder.json:2-16)

questions.question: Where is max_heat declared, what is its default, and which code reads it?

facts.fact: EmberConfig declares MAX_HEAT = defineInRange("max_heat", 200, 50, 1000) in the [forge] section of the common spec (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/config/EmberConfig.java:23-24)
the documented default config has max_heat = 200 under [forge] (config/emberforge-common.toml:10-13)
Kotlin HeatMath.addHeat(current, amount) caps heat at EmberConfig.MAX_HEAT.get() (src/main/kotlin/net/ashvale/emberforge/heat/HeatMath.kt:22)
EmberForgeBlockEntity.serverTick burns fuel only while heat + the fuel's heat stays within MAX_HEAT (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:80)

the block entity's ContainerData slot 1 returns MAX_HEAT; the menu exposes it as getMaxHeat and the Kotlin screen scales the heat bar with menu.maxHeat (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:53; src/main/kotlin/net/ashvale/emberforge/client/EmberForgeScreen.kt:32)

negatives.statement: EmberForgeScreen reads EmberConfig.MAX_HEAT itself (it uses menu.maxHeat, synced from the block entity)

questions.question: /emberforge reset komutunu kapatan ayar nerede tanımlanıyor ve nerede kontrol ediliyor?
questions.question_en: Where is the setting that turns off /emberforge reset declared, and where is it checked?

facts.fact: EmberConfig.ALLOW_RESET_COMMAND = define("allow_reset_command", true) in the [debug] section (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/config/EmberConfig.java:31-33)
the documented default config has allow_reset_command = true under [debug] (config/emberforge-common.toml:23-26)

the Kotlin ForgeCommands.register only offers the reset literal when the source has permission level 2 and EmberConfig.ALLOW_RESET_COMMAND.get() is true (src/main/kotlin/net/ashvale/emberforge/command/ForgeCommands.kt:20-22)
ForgeCommands.register is called by the Java event handler ModEvents.onRegisterCommands (RegisterCommandsEvent) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/event/ModEvents.java:20-23)

negatives.statement: ForgeFunctions.resetForges checks allow_reset_command (only the command's requires does)
the /emberforge heat subcommand is also gated by allow_reset_command

questions.question: Which blockstate, block models and textures does the Ember Forge use when it is lit and when it is not?

facts.fact: blockstates/ember_forge.json maps lit=false (four facings, rotated with y) to emberforge:block/ember_forge (src/main/resources/assets/emberforge/blockstates/ember_forge.json:3-6)
lit=true maps to emberforge:block/ember_forge_lit (src/main/resources/assets/emberforge/blockstates/ember_forge.json:7-10)

models/block/ember_forge.json uses parent minecraft:block/orientable with textures emberforge:block/ember_forge_top, _front and _side (src/main/resources/assets/emberforge/models/block/ember_forge.json:2-7)

models/block/ember_forge_lit.json inherits emberforge:block/ember_forge and only swaps the front texture to emberforge:block/ember_forge_front_lit (src/main/resources/assets/emberforge/models/block/ember_forge_lit.json:2-5)
the item model models/item/ember_forge.json only points at the block model (src/main/resources/assets/emberforge/models/item/ember_forge.json:2)
the lit property is switched by EmberForgeBlockEntity.serverTick: LIT = heat > 0 (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:113-116)

questions.question: Kor Ocağı'nın Türkçe ve İngilizce adı hangi anahtarla, hangi dosyalarda tanımlı ve blok kodda nerede kaydediliyor?
questions.question_en: Under which key and in which files are the Kor Ocağı's Turkish and English names defined, and where is the block registered in code?

facts.fact: Turkish: "block.emberforge.ember_forge": "Kor Ocağı" (src/main/resources/assets/emberforge/lang/tr_tr.json:2)
English: "block.emberforge.ember_forge": "Ember Forge" (src/main/resources/assets/emberforge/lang/en_us.json:2)
ModBlocks registers the block as "ember_forge" (emberforge:ember_forge) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/registry/ModBlocks.java:23-28)
ModItems registers its block item with registerSimpleBlockItem(ModBlocks.EMBER_FORGE) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/registry/ModItems.java:20)

the menu title uses a second key, container.emberforge.ember_forge (also "Kor Ocağı" / "Ember Forge"), returned by EmberForgeBlockEntity.getDisplayName (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:172; src/main/resources/assets/emberforge/lang/tr_tr.json:7)

questions.question: How does pressing the Stoke button in the forge screen end up adding heat on the server?

facts.fact: the Kotlin EmberForgeScreen.init adds a gui.emberforge.stoke button whose action is requestStoke() (src/main/kotlin/net/ashvale/emberforge/client/EmberForgeScreen.kt:16-23)
requestStoke sends StokeForgePayload(menu.pos) with PacketDistributor.sendToServer (src/main/kotlin/net/ashvale/emberforge/client/EmberForgeScreen.kt:25-27)
StokeForgePayload is a Java record carrying the forge's BlockPos, type id emberforge:stoke_forge (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/network/StokeForgePayload.java:10-13)

EmberNetwork.register (RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent on the mod bus) registers it play-to-server with EmberNetwork::handleStoke as handler (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/network/EmberNetwork.java:21-25)
handleStoke drops the packet unless the sender has that forge's menu open and is within 8 blocks, then calls forge.stoke(player) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/network/EmberNetwork.java:28-41)

EmberForgeBlockEntity.stoke adds stoke_heat through HeatMath.addHeat (capped at max_heat) and shows message.emberforge.stoked (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:140-144)

negatives.statement: the client screen calls EmberForgeBlockEntity.stoke itself
the server side sends the payload (direction reversed)

questions.question: Kor Ocağı'nın blok varlığı her tick'te ne yapıyor?
questions.question_en: What does the Ember Forge's block entity do on every tick?

facts.fact: EmberForgeBlock.getTicker installs EmberForgeBlockEntity::serverTick, on the server side only (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlock.java:70-73)
it burns one item from the fuel slot when HeatMath.heatForFuel gives heat and the total stays within max_heat (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:78-84)
every 40 game ticks it adds 2 heat if the block below is in #emberforge:forge_heat_sources (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:86-89)

it looks up an emberforge:forging recipe for the input slot; if the output fits it adds HeatMath.progressPerTick(heat, minHeat) to progress and finishes (one input -> result) at forge_time, otherwise progress drops to 0 (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:91-105)
it cools by 1 heat every decay_interval_ticks game ticks via cooled() (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:107-111, 123-125)
it sets the block's LIT property to heat > 0 (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:113-116)

questions.question: What does /emberforge reset do, from the command down to the data pack?

facts.fact: the Kotlin command tree in ForgeCommands.register runs ForgeFunctions.resetForges(ctx.source) for the reset literal (src/main/kotlin/net/ashvale/emberforge/command/ForgeCommands.kt:20-22)

Java ForgeFunctions.resetForges checks that the function exists and runs it with server.getCommands().performPrefixedCommand(source, "function " + RESET_FORGES) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/util/ForgeFunctions.java:16-25)
RESET_FORGES is "emberforge:debug/reset_forges", i.e. src/main/resources/data/emberforge/function/debug/reset_forges.mcfunction (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/util/ForgeFunctions.java:10)
the function replaces every emberforge:ember_forge within 16 blocks with an unlit one carrying {Heat:0,Progress:0} (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/function/debug/reset_forges.mcfunction:1-2)

those NBT keys are what EmberForgeBlockEntity.loadAdditional reads back (Heat, Progress; the absent Items tag leaves the inventory empty) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/block/EmberForgeBlockEntity.java:146-152)

it then warns when a #emberforge:forge_heat_sources block is under the executor and prints message.emberforge.reset.done (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/function/debug/reset_forges.mcfunction:3-4)

negatives.statement: the command changes the forges' block entities directly (it goes through the data-pack function)
ModEvents.onRegisterCommands calls resetForges (it only registers the command tree)

questions.question: emberforge:rewards/first_cinder fonksiyonu nereden çalıştırılıyor?
questions.question_en: Where is the emberforge:rewards/first_cinder function run from?

facts.fact: only from the advancement advancement/first_cinder.json, as its reward: "rewards": {"function": "emberforge:rewards/first_cinder"} (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/advancement/first_cinder.json:27-29)
that advancement is granted by minecraft:inventory_changed once the player holds an item from #emberforge:cinder_ores (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/advancement/first_cinder.json:15-26)
the item tag #emberforge:cinder_ores contains emberforge:cinder_ore (src/main/resources/data/emberforge/tags/item/cinder_ores.json:3-5)

negatives.statement: Java or Kotlin code runs emberforge:rewards/first_cinder (only the advancement reward does)

questions.question: Where are the mod's block entity type, menu type and recipe serializer registered, and where are those registers attached to the mod event bus?

facts.fact: ModBlocks.EMBER_FORGE_ENTITY: BLOCK_ENTITIES.register("ember_forge", ...) with BlockEntityType.Builder.of(EmberForgeBlockEntity::new, EMBER_FORGE.get()) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/registry/ModBlocks.java:34-36)
ModMenus.EMBER_FORGE: MENUS.register("ember_forge", () -> IMenuTypeExtension.create(EmberForgeMenu::new)) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/registry/ModMenus.java:15-16)
ModRecipes.FORGING_SERIALIZER: RECIPE_SERIALIZERS.register("forging", ForgingRecipe.Serializer::new) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/registry/ModRecipes.java:20-21)

the @Mod constructor EmberForge(IEventBus modBus, ModContainer) registers every DeferredRegister on the mod bus, e.g. ModBlocks.BLOCK_ENTITIES.register(modBus), ModMenus.MENUS.register(modBus), ModRecipes.RECIPE_SERIALIZERS.register(modBus) (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/EmberForge.java:21-28)
on the client, ClientSetup.registerScreens binds the menu type to the Kotlin EmberForgeScreen (src/main/java/net/ashvale/emberforge/client/ClientSetup.java:15-18)

negatives.statement: a ModBlockEntities class registers the block entity type (there is none; it is in ModBlocks)
